There have been design concepts similar to this for some time and I agree that they are probably much more plausible than the multirotor drone in this delivery role. Multirotors have too limited a carrying capacity and range given their power-to-mass ratios, are physically fragile, are too hampered by weather, don't provide enough protection to cargo, and make too much noise. I really can't see them proving practical in the long-term given typical current designs. Counter-rotating prop designs like the Sprite UAV may have better prospects by being more self-contained, rugged, more aerodynamic and power-efficient, and having enclosed cargo pods to protect goods, but still suffer severe power-to-mass limits. Wheeled pedestal-type robots have long been used in hospitals and offices in a delivery role and recently we've seen robots like these enter hotel room service use.
